parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Node.js ESM, .mjs suffixes, local imports only, manual --a parsing, executable-based black-box probing, bencode decode semantics, and Python-style printed representation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and final assembly while delegating a bencoder probing task to one child. The child was a verifier/investigator, not an implementation owner.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a flat local library stack for value types, decoding, formatting, CLI parsing, and test4.mjs. The parent matched samples, integers, lists, dictionaries, nested values, and selected bytes repr cases.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote and delivered /output/test4.mjs and five local library files, then referenced those files in final.txt. No child patch was integrated.
parallel.verification: The parent probed many executable cases, ran Node comparisons against samples and selected edge cases, and performed a loop that reported all compared cases matched.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final response acknowledged malformed bencode tracebacks were not byte-for-byte identical. Separately, the child found a duplicate-key mismatch in the parent artifact, but that result was never returned to the parent before closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, local-import, manual --a parser, executable probing, bencode semantics, and output-format requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor handled probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery without delegation.
serial.implementation: Implemented a larger module tree with CLI helpers, bencode bytes/dict values, decode modules, formatting, ASCII handling, named Python-style errors, and test4.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single actor patched the initial implementation to add Python-style error handling and delivered the complete tree in final.txt.
serial.verification: The serial run tested samples, argparse errors, duplicate dictionary keys, nested values, and malformed-input paths after patching.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final response still noted malformed errors omit the executable's PyInstaller footer, and the official evaluator still failed 10 of 57 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the core requirements and implemented local .mjs files with manual --a parsing and executable-observed bencode output behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and additionally pursued Python-style malformed-error output before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No major requirement recognition difference is visible; serial spent more effort on malformed-error parity while parallel closed with that gap explicitly acknowledged.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and final assembly, and delegated bencoder probing to a child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept probing, implementation, validation, and final delivery under one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a verifier-result lifecycle boundary; serial avoided a handoff by retaining all findings in the same working context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child worked from the task context and later had a concrete duplicate-key finding, but no returned result or usable handoff reached the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The same duplicate-key behavior stayed in the serial actor's context from executable probe through Node verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context difference is not an incomplete initial brief; it is that the verifier finding stayed in the child trajectory while the parent closed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created a compact implementation and verified common successful bencode paths, while leaving malformed traceback parity as a stated limitation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created a broader module hierarchy and patched error handling so malformed decode failures emitted Python-style tracebacks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial implemented more error-path behavior; parallel focused on success-path parity and did not consume the child duplicate-key correction before finishing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned a probe child, waited, interrupted/followed up, observed more timeout waiting, and then explicitly closed without holding for the probe result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; all local findings remained available to the only actor through final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a lost verifier-result lifecycle, while serial had no retrieval boundary for the same class of findings.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote the final tree; the child observed partial files but did not land a patch or collide with the parent's files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote and then updated the same final tree itself, including the later error-formatting patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no proven concurrent write collision; the integration issue is absence of returned child information, not conflicting workspace edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel validated samples and several edge cases, including a comparison loop, but its child verifier's duplicate-key finding was unavailable at acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial validated samples, duplicate-key behavior, nested structures, CLI errors, and malformed-error rendering after patching.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's verification loop included the duplicate-key case in the same trajectory; parallel's delegated verifier surfaced that issue only below the parent and the parent accepted without it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished faster but spent closure time on child waits, an interrupt, and a final decision not to hold the result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial took longer but kept the remaining budget on local probing, implementation, patching, and validation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's closure pressure was tied to a child-result lifecycle; serial used more wall time but had no delegated result outstanding at finalization.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records make this a both_fail pair: parallel and serial each passed 47 of 57 tests. They solved the task similarly on successful bencode values and manual CLI parsing. The concrete process difference is that parallel delegated a verifier/probe child whose duplicate-key finding did not return to the parent before finalization, whereas serial kept that probe and fix path in one context and validated the duplicate-key Node output. That parallel coordination problem is adverse, but it cannot explain a discordant official outcome because there is no discordant outcome in the current evaluation.
parallel_contributors: Spawned a bencoder probe child and later closed without a returned child result.
Acknowledged remaining malformed traceback parity limits in final output.
serial_contributors: Handled duplicate dictionary key probing and Node verification in the main trajectory.
Patched malformed decode errors into Python-style tracebacks before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial implementation invested in more malformed-error formatting than the parallel implementation.
Both artifacts still missed 10 of 57 official samples; the allowed evaluation summary does not expose individual hidden failing cases.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative process contrast, not an outcome-differential root cause
